controlName: Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk Management
purpose: Ensures AI risks arising from third-party software, data, and other supply chain elements are addressed through deliberate policy rather than assumed away.
summary: Policies and procedures are in place to address AI risks and benefits arising from third-party software, data, and other supply chain issues, including contractual requirements for third parties and contingency processes for when third-party AI components fail or introduce risk.
expectedStatementElements: How third-party AI software, models, and data sources are vetted before adoption
What contractual requirements govern third-party AI risk responsibilities
What contingency plans exist if a third-party AI component fails, is deprecated, or introduces unacceptable risk
How the organization tracks which AI systems depend on third-party components
evidenceExamples: Third-party AI vendor risk assessment or vetting checklist
Contract language specifying AI risk responsibilities for vendors
Contingency plan for third-party AI component failure or deprecation
Inventory mapping AI systems to their third-party dependencies
commonGaps: Third-party AI models or data are adopted without any formal risk vetting
Contracts with AI vendors don't address risk responsibilities or liability
No contingency plan exists if a critical third-party AI dependency is deprecated or fails
No inventory tracks which systems rely on which third-party AI components
interviewQuestions: How do you vet a third-party AI vendor or model before adopting it?
What does your contract with an AI vendor say about who's responsible if something goes wrong?
What would you do if a third-party AI component you depend on was suddenly deprecated?
Can you trace which of your systems depend on which third-party AI components?
